name: Russ Tedrake
notice: Simulation based on public material; not the person's own words.

D01.one_line: Not my specialty; foundation models trained without compute at scale are mostly scaled-down versions, with limited weight for industry
D01.late_modes: Merely reproducing larger-scale pre-training is already too late; academia cannot beat industry on compute

D02.one_line: LLM reasoning/RLVR is not my specialty; by analogy with robot RL, algorithmic innovation often originates in academia, but the window is narrowing
D02.late_modes: Chasing RLVR fine-tuning scores on off-the-shelf benchmarks is already too late; top labs overwhelm it with resources

D03.one_line: I make no judgment on agent self-improvement itself; but whether autonomous improvement is really more effective than compute spending has not yet been statistically validated

D04.one_line: Not my specialty; conclusions about scaffolding being absorbed by models are inconsistent across benchmarks and should be settled by rigorous evaluation
D04.late_modes: Building general agent scaffolding is already too late; vendor CLI agents already fill the top of the leaderboards

D05.one_line: Evaluation is a bottleneck I have validated repeatedly: a real robot cannot rerun the same experiment, so statistical design is scarcer than the model itself
D05.late_modes: Chasing a single static benchmark leaderboard is already too late; design work on evaluation methodology itself is not too late
D05.conflict: Author of the LBM evaluation and also CEO of Walden

D06.one_line: My home field; low-cost hardware is loosening the old constraint that real-robot trials are scarce, but the ability to design evaluations is still the bar
D06.late_modes: Reproducing viral demo videos that 'look like they get work done' is already too late; single-task showcases without statistical validation are worth little
D06.conflict: Founder and CEO of Walden; direct commercial interest lies here

D07.one_line: The evidence shows the diffusion head is not the only optimum; the paradigm dispute is unsettled
D07.late_modes: Swapping in a new action head to chase benchmarks is already too late; work that does not address data/evaluation has low value
D07.conflict: Founder and CEO; the company bets on the diffusion/LBM route

D08.one_line: 'Looks realistic' and 'physically correct' are often confused; I trust world models that are action-conditioned and statistically validated more
D08.late_modes: Chasing only higher resolution/longer consistency in quality metrics is already too late; demo videos without closed-loop decision validation are of doubtful value
D08.conflict: Walden's business model depends indirectly on this judgment

D09.one_line: Whether simulation can substitute for real-robot trials depends on whether it has been validated as correlated with the real world, not on how high its resolution is
D09.late_modes: Showing only that something 'runs in simulation' with no correlation validation is already too late; claims of 'unlimited data' that cannot be quantified have no value
D09.conflict: Simulation cost directly affects his company's unit economics

D10.one_line: No judgment: autonomous-driving evaluation is not a field I have discussed publicly, although problems like self-reported, not independently audited data are isomorphic to my own skepticism

D11.one_line: I am a downstream consumer; the spatial-reasoning gap is a concrete bottleneck for robot manipulation, and diagnostic work is worth more than leaderboard chasing
D11.late_modes: Chasing scores with general VLMs is already too late, overwhelmed by top labs' resources; specialized spatial/3D diagnosis is not too late

D12.one_line: Not my track; evaluation driven by image quality has fragile value, but the methodology for generative-distribution fidelity shares its roots with mine
D12.late_modes: A pure quality/FID race is already too late; generation evaluation not tied to downstream tasks is of doubtful value

D13.one_line: No judgment: alignment and interpretability are not my specialty, and the material has no relevant public statements

D14.one_line: Inference latency/throughput directly affects robot deployment cost; it is an engineering parameter I care about, but not a research specialty
D14.conflict: Falling compute costs benefit his company

D15.one_line: No judgment: no public material shows me discussing AI for Science, and it has no direct overlap with my methodology

D16.one_line: No judgment: recommender systems are not my specialty and the material does not cover them

lever_reason: Evaluation/verification decides whether any claim can be trusted; simulation, world models and real data together address the hard constraint that real-robot experiments cannot be repeated; scaled-up pre-training is not the main lever for physical AI.

Q2.condition: Narrow domain, not general LLM pre-training; credible third-party evaluation; a complementary team of 2-4 people; open model weights with a path to outside adoption.

cruxes.question: Must an action policy use diffusion/flow to represent multimodality, or is continuous regression enough?
cruxes.my_position: Diffusion is useful but not the only solution; OpenVLA-OFT shows continuous actions + parallel decoding can overtake it
cruxes.would_change_if: More independent teams consistently show continuous actions outperforming diffusion in larger-scale real-robot evaluations

cruxes.question: Can pure video generation implicitly learn enough physics to serve as a world model?
cruxes.my_position: Skeptical; 'looks real' does not equal 'physically correct', which requires action-conditioned models + statistical validation on real robots
cruxes.would_change_if: Reproducible, strong evidence that video world models generalize out of distribution in physics, not just similarity matching

cruxes.question: Is evaluation methodology really the bottleneck of physical-AI progress, or an excuse for the compute gap?
cruxes.my_position: It is a bottleneck: without statistical design you cannot even tell which route is better, so this is not an excuse
cruxes.would_change_if: Some route keeps succeeding in large-scale real deployment even without rigorous evaluation, which would show that statistical design is not necessary

taste_advice: First ask whether a known structure can be used; only when there is no structure and plenty of data is it the generative model's turn; whichever road you take, without a statistically credible evaluation you know nothing.

pairwise.why: Evaluation is the precondition for every judgment; without it even the claims about D08 cannot be verified
Without evaluation methodology, claims of robot progress cannot be verified; D05 is more upstream
D06 has twenty years of verifiable real-deployment evidence, while D08 is still mostly demos and inference
Action representations already have statistical validation on real robots (LBM), while D08 mostly remains at simulation/demo level
D06 is the end goal; D09 (simulation) is a tool that serves it and not a destination in itself
Whether self-improvement really works has not been statistically validated, which is closer to my methodology
The spatial-reasoning gap is a bottleneck robots actually run into; multimodal generation quality is not directly relevant
For the evaluation-bottleneck judgment I have twenty years of first-hand evidence; pre-training scaling is not my specialty
The sample-efficiency problem of self-improvement is closer to an unsolved scientific problem than scaffolding engineering is
No public material supports my judgment on alignment/interpretability; I have first-hand experience in evaluation
The autonomous-driving evaluation system is not a field I know well; robot manipulation is my home field
